preconditions.description: The input `s` must be a string.

postconditions.description: The output string contains only alphabetic characters (no numeric characters).

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == sum(int(s[i]) if s[i].isdigit() else 1 for i in range(len(s)) if i == 0 or not s[i-1].isdigit() or (i > 0 and s[i-1].isdigit() and not s[i-2].isdigit()))
postconditions.description: The output length is the sum of the numeric values (interpreted as counts) preceding each alphabetic character, where consecutive numeric characters are ignored (only the first is considered). If no numeric value precedes an alphabetic character, it is counted once.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] == s[j] for i in range(len(return_value)) for j in range(len(s)) if s[j].isalpha() and (i // (int(s[k]) if s[k].isdigit() else 1 for k in range(j) if k == 0 or not s[k-1].isdigit() or (k > 0 and s[k-1].isdigit() and not s[k-2].isdigit())) == j))
postconditions.description: The output string is constructed by repeating each alphabetic character in `s` according to the preceding numeric value (ignoring consecutive numeric characters), and the order of characters in the output matches their order in `s`.
If the input string `s` is empty, the output is also an empty string.
